exposure: SARS-CoV-2 infection at the time of birth
outcome: Maternal and neonatal length of hospital stay after birth
cohort: 342,080 women with a recorded singleton birth between May 29, 2020, and January 31, 2021, in England
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection at the time of birth is associated with higher rates of fetal death, preterm birth, preeclampsia, and emergency cesarean delivery, but no additional adverse neonatal outcomes were observed beyond those related to preterm delivery.
mod_finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection at the time of birth was associated with a higher risk of emergency cesarean delivery (adjusted odds ratio, 1.63; 95% confidence interval, 1.51-1.76; P<.001).
gest_age: Singleton births between May 29, 2020, and January 31, 2021
